title: Chinese Table Manners
synopsis: Learn the essentials of Chinese dining etiquette.

fullText.simplified:
中国人的吃饭礼仪

    在中国，你知道吃饭的时候什么能做，什么不能做吗？今天，我们就来说说中国人的吃饭礼仪。
    和老人在一起吃饭时，我们应该让年纪大的人先入座。吃完要离开餐桌时，也要等老人离开后才能离开。这是尊敬老人的一种表现。
    一般很多人在一起吃饭时，大家会坐圆桌。圆桌中间放旋转转盘，菜会放到旋转转盘上。你想要吃什么菜就可以轻轻地旋转转盘，把那个菜转到你面前。站起来夹别人面前的菜是很不礼貌的。
    在正式场合吃饭的时候，我们夹菜和喝汤都会用公筷和公勺。公筷就是饭桌上公共使用的筷子，同样的，公勺就是公共使用的勺子。如果你想夹菜或喝汤，就必须使用公筷或公勺，把菜或汤放到自己碗里，然后再用自己的筷子和勺子吃。这样就能避免吃到别人的口水，非常卫生。
    最后一件在饭桌上不能做的事情是：筷子不能插在米饭上。因为这样做看起来很像中国人供奉祖先时的上香，所以很不吉利。
    那么多的吃饭礼仪，你学会了吗？
fullText.traditional:
中國人的吃飯禮儀

    在中國，你知道吃飯的時候什麼能做，什麼不能做嗎？今天，我們就來說說中國人的吃飯禮儀。
    和老人在一起吃飯時，我們應該讓年紀大的人先入座。吃完要離開餐桌時，也要等老人離開後才能離開。這是尊敬老人的一種表現。
    一般很多人在一起吃飯時，大家會坐圓桌。圓桌中間放旋轉轉盤，菜會放到旋轉轉盤上。你想要吃什麼菜就可以輕輕地旋轉轉盤，把那個菜轉到你面前。站起來夾別人面前的菜是很不禮貌的。
    在正式場合吃飯的時候，我們夾菜和喝湯都會用公筷和公勺。公筷就是飯桌上公共使用的筷子，同樣的，公勺就是公共使用的勺子。如果你想夾菜或喝湯，就必須使用公筷或公勺，把菜或湯放到自己碗裡，然後再用自己的筷子和勺子吃。這樣就能避免吃到別人的口水，非常衛生。
    最後一件在飯桌上不能做的事情是：筷子不能插在米飯上。因為這樣做看起來很像中國人供奉祖先時的上香，所以很不吉利。
    那麼多的吃飯禮儀，你學會了嗎？

sentences.pinyin: jīn tiān wǒ men jiù lái shuō shuo zhōng guó rén de chī fàn lǐ yí
sentences.english: Do you know what you can do and what you cannot do while eating in China?
Today, let’s talk about Chinese table manners.

sentences.simplified: 和老人在一起吃饭时，我们应该让年纪大的人先入座。
sentences.traditional: 和老人在一起吃飯時，我們應該讓年紀大的人先入座。
sentences.pinyin: hé lǎo rén zài yì qǐ chī fàn shí wǒ men yīng gāi ràng nián jì dà de rén xiān rù zuò

sentences.simplified: 吃完要离开餐桌时，也要等老人离开后才能离开。
sentences.traditional: 吃完要離開餐桌時，也要等老人離開後才能離開。
sentences.pinyin: chī wán yào lí kāi cān zhuō shí yě yào děng lǎo rén lí kāi hòu cái néng lí kāi
sentences.english: When eating with elders, we should let those who are older get seated first.

sentences.simplified: 这是尊敬老人的一种表现。
sentences.traditional: 這是尊敬老人的一種表現。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shì zūn jìng lǎo rén de yì zhǒng biǎo xiàn
sentences.english: When we’re finished eating and want to leave the table, we also need to wait for the elders to leave before leaving.
This is a sign of respect towards elders.

sentences.simplified: 一般很多人在一起吃饭时，大家会坐圆桌。
sentences.traditional: 一般很多人在一起吃飯時，大家會坐圓桌。
sentences.pinyin: yì bān hěn duō rén zài yì qǐ chī fàn shí dà jiā huì zuò yuán zhuō

sentences.simplified: 圆桌中间放旋转转盘，菜会放到旋转转盘上。
sentences.traditional: 圓桌中間放旋轉轉盤，菜會放到旋轉轉盤上。
sentences.pinyin: yuán zhuō zhōng jiān fàng xuán zhuǎn zhuàn pán cài huì fàng dào xuán zhuǎn zhuàn pán shang
sentences.english: Usually when a lot of people eat together, they will sit at a round table.

sentences.simplified: 你想要吃什么菜就可以轻轻地旋转转盘，把那个菜转到你面前。
sentences.traditional: 你想要吃什麼菜就可以輕輕地旋轉轉盤，把那個菜轉到你面前。
sentences.pinyin: nǐ xiǎng yào chī shén me cài jiù kě yǐ qīng qīng de xuán zhuǎn zhuàn pán bǎ nà ge cài zhuàn dào nǐ miàn qián
sentences.english: In the middle of the round table there is a Lazy Susan, and the dishes will be placed on this Lazy Susan.

sentences.simplified: 站起来夹别人面前的菜是很不礼貌的。
sentences.traditional: 站起來夾別人面前的菜是很不禮貌的。
sentences.pinyin: zhàn qǐ lái jiā bié ren miàn qián de cài shì hěn bù lǐ mào de
sentences.english: When you want to eat a dish, you can gently turn the Lazy Susan to bring that dish in front of you.
Standing up to get food from a dish that is in front of someone else is very impolite.

sentences.simplified: 在正式场合吃饭的时候，我们夹菜和喝汤都会用公筷和公勺。
sentences.traditional: 在正式場合吃飯的時候，我們夾菜和喝湯都會用公筷和公勺。
sentences.pinyin: zài zhèng shì chǎng hé chī fàn de shí hou wǒ men jiā cài hé hē tāng dōu huì yòng gōng kuài hé gōng sháo

sentences.simplified: 公筷就是饭桌上公共使用的筷子，

sentences.english: When eating in formal settings, we will often use serving chopsticks and serving spoons to pick up food and serve soup.

sentences.simplified: 同样的，公勺就是公共使用的勺子。
sentences.traditional: 同樣的，公勺就是公共使用的勺子。
sentences.pinyin: tóng yàng de gōng sháo jiù shì gōng gòng shǐ yòng de sháo zi
sentences.english: Serving chopsticks are chopsticks that are used communally at the table.

sentences.simplified: 如果你想夹菜或喝汤，
sentences.traditional: 如果你想夾菜或喝湯，

sentences.english: Likewise, serving spoons are spoons that are used communally.

sentences.english: If you wish to pick up food or serve soup, ..

sentences.simplified: 然后再用自己的筷子和勺子吃。
sentences.traditional: 然後再用自己的筷子和勺子吃。

sentences.simplified: 这样就能避免吃到别人的口水，非常卫生。
sentences.traditional: 這樣就能避免吃到別人的口水，非常衛生。
sentences.pinyin: zhè yàng jiù néng bì miǎn chī dào bié ren de kǒu shuǐ fēi cháng wèi shēng
sentences.english: Then you use your own chopsticks or spoon to eat.
This is very sanitary as we can avoid eating other people’s saliva.

sentences.traditional: 最後一件在飯桌上不能做的事情是：筷子不能插在米飯上。

sentences.traditional: 因為這樣做看起來很像中國人供奉祖先時的上香，所以很不吉利。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi zhè yàng zuò kàn qǐ lái hěn xiàng zhōng guó rén gòng fèng zǔ xiān shí de shàng xiāng suǒ yǐ hěn bù jí lì
sentences.english: The last thing that you cannot do at the table: you cannot stick your chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice.
This looks very similar to the incense Chinese people offer to their ancestors, so it’s very inauspicious.

raw.synopsis: Learn the essentials of Chinese dining etiquette.
sentence_translations: Chinese Table Manners
Do you know what you can do and what you cannot do while eating in China?
Today, let’s talk about Chinese table manners.
When eating with elders, we should let those who are older get seated first.
When we’re finished eating and want to leave the table, we also need to wait for the elders to leave before leaving.
This is a sign of respect towards elders.
Usually when a lot of people eat together, they will sit at a round table.
In the middle of the round table there is a Lazy Susan, and the dishes will be placed on this Lazy Susan.
When you want to eat a dish, you can gently turn the Lazy Susan to bring that dish in front of you.
Standing up to get food from a dish that is in front of someone else is very impolite.
When eating in formal settings, we will often use serving chopsticks and serving spoons to pick up food and serve soup.
Serving chopsticks are chopsticks that are used communally at the table.
Likewise, serving spoons are spoons that are used communally.
If you wish to pick up food or serve soup, ..
.. then you must use the serving chopsticks or the serving spoon to bring the food or soup into your own bowl.
Then you use your own chopsticks or spoon to eat.
This is very sanitary as we can avoid eating other people’s saliva.
The last thing that you cannot do at the table: you cannot stick your chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice.
This looks very similar to the incense Chinese people offer to their ancestors, so it’s very inauspicious.
So many different table manners! Have you mastered them?
